newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Judge strikes down California term limits.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Judge strikes down California term limits.

text.p: A federal judge Wednesday struck down California's term limits law which restricted the number of times state legislators may run for office.

U.S. District Judge Claudia Wilken of Oakland said the term limits law, passed by California voters in 1990, imposed "a severe burden" on constitutionally-protected rights of voting, expression and association.

"The state has not established that life-time term limits are narrowly tailored to serve a compelling state interest. The court therefore declares that the lifetime term limits provisions ... violate the U.S. Constitution," Wilken said in a 54-page ruling.

Term limits transformed California politics by limiting state senators to two four-year terms and assembly members to three two-year terms. Many veteran politicians have been forced out of office by term limits.
The California Supreme Court had previously ruled that the state's term limits law did not violate the U.S. constitution.
Several state legislators and their supporters sued California Secretary of State Bill Jones and local electoral officials in 1995 to challenge the term limits law.
